newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - Prices still struggling.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - Prices still struggling.

text.p: India's second tender for the purchase of diesel for January delivery has raised spirits in the Gulf refined oil products market, but traders on Thursday were bearish on prospects for stronger prices.
"Indian Oil Corp's supplementary tender has raised spirits," said one. "But the market still has a bearish overtone, even with the Far East picking up a little bit."
"The supplementary tender may change notions," said another.
The tender, offered late last month, requests offers of 40,000-45,000-tonne cargoes of 0.5 percent sulphur diesel for delivery to the west coast port of Kandla.
India had previously bought in a tender a modest 255,000 tonnes of diesel for delivery in January, down from initial expectations of 700,000 tonnes.
"IOC was the biggest buyer. When the amount was that low it suggests we have got to move elsewhere. The premium should be relatively weak relative to the whole year," said another trader.
One trader said one percent gas oil appeared to be balancing out, with premiums at about 50 cents, steady at last week's level.
"There has not been much difference with the 0.5 percent grade in terms of premiums," he said.
"In terms of middle distillates, gas oil is becoming more balanced," said one, attributing the development to barrels moving out of the region to Singapore.
"This has taken excess production away," he said.
But he said jet was "on the long side of balance".
One trader pinned hopes on low inventories in east Africa and the Indian subcontinent, but he said the market remained bearish.
Gas oil was assessed at $30.50/$30.70 a barrel fob on Thursday from the previous week's $29.80/30.00 and jet was at $31.20/$31.40 from $31.60/90.
The Fujairah bunker market seemed to gain momentum. 380-cst bunker fuel from the Gulf port was assessed on Thursday at $117 a tonne, compared to last week's $116. 180-cst was at $125, up from $122.
